cells.tense: The persistence is fully here now, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: persist on your own reserves through the pressure
cells.ask: Pick the part of the shared work that leans hardest on what you've already got, and carry it on your own reserves, asking no one to prop you up.
cells.core:
What you believe in has been going long enough that you keep it without effort. The shared practices and the ordinary days around them hold because you keep showing up, and you do it from what is already in you rather than from anything fresh promised. That is why the tradition stays warm instead of merely correct.

What this balance feeds next is your own share of the work, carried on your own reserves. Pick the part that leans hardest on what is already in you, and carry just that through the week — no wider, no longer — while everything else stays where it is. You find out which reserves are real, and the whole thing is lighter for one piece held plainly.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it going out of what is already in you.
cells.verb: to keep going after the thing has finished
cells.place: inside a tradition that already carries your hands

cells.tense: You will brace against a season that cannot be written in yet.
cells.act: keep the truth a while before saying it
cells.ask: Before you bring one thing to the group, keep it for a day, and say the version that still holds.
cells.core:
The tradition is being built into years nobody has seen. Plans, materials, the way it will run — all of it going up before the actual day, and the going is getting heavier. Some of that care is real. The pace is outrunning what the group can carry.

Before you bring one thing to the group, keep it for a day, and say the version that still holds. That pause is the whole ask, and it costs nothing you have to spare. What is worth saying survives the waiting; the rest goes back to being yours a little longer, and the next stretch shows itself without being pre-built over.

cells.tense: You were still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Look after one small piece of the tradition that still has life in it, with a steady hand — gently, and without holding on tight.
cells.core:
The shared tradition is still there. You are not in it. The rituals happen around you, and the part of you that used to reach for them isn't reaching. You can still say why it mattered. You say it from outside the door, and the reciting is what you do instead of standing inside.

Look after one small piece of it that still has life in it, with a steady hand — gently, without holding on tight. That is the whole ask. What gets tended this way grows back in time, and this small piece feeds the same persistence that once carried the whole of it. The shine returns through the practice, not before it.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you have been writing in.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: When the shared work comes up, claim one piece of it as yours — the practical thing you do — and say nothing more about it.
cells.core:
The shared thing holds partly because you hold it. You carry your share of the practical weight — the showing up, the small repairs, the part nobody assigns — and your account leaves that out. You'd say the practice holds itself. Others lean on it every week and have no reason to disagree.

Underneath this is something you started once because you wanted to, before it became the thing loads rest on. When the shared work comes up, claim one piece of it as yours — the practical thing you do — and say nothing more. No speech, no credit. The record then shows the hand that was already there.
cells.sheetLine: You say it is the tradition's work. Some of it is yours.

attempts.check: The record does not support naming what the person has been carrying through the shared tradition — a season, a loss, a family situation — so the Too Little cell locates them at a door already passed and says nothing about what happened there. The reader could reasonably say the tiredness is about the tradition itself rather than about persistence inside it, and the Too Much reader could say the building ahead is not anxiety but genuine responsibility; the asks are still useful in both cases because each is one visible act inside the seat, not a verdict on the person. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you still hold it up' — it admires the endurance instead of describing it, so it is cut and the ordinary version is kept.
